BUFFALO CITY MUNICIPALITY

By: Catherine Rice | Paid

Proposal


Show:

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
An Eastern Cape development agency mandated to attract investors and increase economic development has come under the spotlight for a series of stalled multi-million rand projects.

Unique Selling Point:
An Eastern Cape development agency, the Buffalo City Metropolitan Development Agency, has a series of failed multi-million rand projects on its track record. The BCMDA is funded by the Buffalo City Metropolitan Municipality to increase economic development and tourism. The Municipality has ploughed millions into its projects, but some have stalled, while others that have been completed have raised serious questions about why they cost so much.

Summary:
The Buffalo City Metropolitan Municipality in the Eastern Cape is yet another municipality in South Africa that is failing to deliver services to its residents. Sewage spills have become commonplace, potholes pepper the roads, water cuts and poor water quality … these are just some of the issues residents deal with on a daily basis.
Abandoned, hijacked buildings in the East London City Centre have become an eyesore and are fuelling crime. Driving through the centre, the dereliction and decay is visible everywhere. It’s clear the municipality is cash-strapped. But, that hasn’t stopped the Buffalo City Metropolitan Development Agency from cashing in on a number of multi million rand projects. The BCMDA is meant to drive development in the area, and its projects are funded by the Municipality. In this insert, we look at the BCMDA – and some of the multimillion rand projects its been involved in. In November last year, it unveiled a beachfront upgrade, that the EFF dubbed “The Stoep”. The project costs ballooned to R100 million and what was presented to council is not what was delivered. It is also involved in the upgrade of the Waterworld park which has cost R121 million to date. This project has completely stalled, and the BCMDA now says it needs over R40 million to complete it. The Victoria Grounds in Qonce, formerly King Williams Town, is also a project on BCMDA's books. They planned to demolish it and build a mall there and multi-use facility, but even that has stalled, despite a developer being contracted to do the job. The sports stadium, which has huge historical significance, has become a shell of what it once was and has been completely stripped. The ANC run municipality has been asked for reports on these projects, but are simply ignored. Opposition councillors say it’s impossible to get any information out of those in charge. In an attempt to find answers, we confront the Municipality. Both the current and former Mayor refused to do an interview with us. The BCMDA CEO cancelled a scheduled interview at the last minute, and instead Municipality spokesperson Samwelo Ngwenya was tasked with answering our questions on behalf of both the Municipality and the BCMDA.

NATSOUND

VO 1 The year is 1977 - the date is the 25th of September …the funeral of anti-apartheid activist Steve Biko is taking place..

VO 2 It’s a seminal moment in South Africa’s history … murdered by Apartheid security police officers…Biko becomes a symbol of the Struggle.

VO 3 Thousands attend his funeral at the Victoria Grounds in King William’s Town …. (Visuals from Gallo)

VO 4 You would think a place of such historical significance would be cherished….you’d be wrong (fast cuts, montage of the dereliction)

GOVAN Clip 543 / Day 2 Time code 16:28 Tell me when did the stripping of this place start?
UPSOUND Thembani Tom / King Sports Veterans Association Clip 543 / Day 2 Time code: It started long time. By 2018, the ground floor was already being stripped, everything the copper tubings were not there the showers and the wash basins were not there, only thing that was left there was the top side of this pavilion.
GOVAN: When was last part of the stripping done here?.
THEMBANI: Last month.

VO 5 Thembani Tom is fighting for the restoration of these grounds… Stripped and looted in broad daylight, the Victoria Grounds are a shell of what they once were.. (WhatsApped you cellphone visuals and photos.)

UPSOUND Thembani Tom Clip 543 / Day 2 Time code: 11:38 Why this roof was taken during the daylight. And not even a single person is arrested.

VO 6 Qonce, formerly King Williams Town, is where I grew up. Victoria Grounds was where I often played rugby as a teenager. Coming back here, I can’t believe what I am seeing.

LINK (Day 2 / Clip 592) I’ve always wanted to do a homecoming episode on Carte Blanche. I just didn’t imagine that this would be it. Unfortunately, my hometown is being systematically destroyed and there’s no better example than the Victoria Grounds.

VO 7 Walking through what is left of the structures on Victoria Grounds, unlocks so many memories for me..

NATSOUND Govan Clip 569 These change rooms I used to visit when I was a kid.

VO 8 There is nothing left, every last pipe has been stolen … it’s become a dangerous place…inhabited by nyaope addicts… locals call them Ama Para.

NATSOUND Clip 568
Thembani 01:05 People can be raped here. People can be mugged here. And the government is just keeping quiet. People say I’m critical.
(Guy walks in)
Govan: Do you stay here?
Guy says “I wash cars”
Govan: You sleep here? Is this place dangerous?
Guys says “Not for me”
Thembani: But its dangerous for other people.
Guy says “Its too much dangerous for other people. I’m connected with the para para…I’m shocked when I see you here. That camera they are going using, they going to take. Let me go.
Thembani: That is from the horse’s mouth

VO 9 This is a microcosm - an affliction happening across the Buffalo City Metropolitan Municipality (visuals of post office in King Williams Town) The charred remains of the post office in King Williams Town testament to the dilapidation of the area.

VO 10 Not even the city of East London has been spared.

(Clip Welcome to East London sign / end of day three / Clip 730 onwards)

VO 11 Abandoned buildings have become havens for criminals.

VO 12 The deterioration of East London is visible on every street corner.. It’s not the place I remember from my student days.

LINK (Clip 536 / Day 1) I used to walk this route ten years ago freely. Now it feels like I’m in the Joburg CBD. It’s not safe and the City seems to be rotting away.

VO 13 So where is the Municipality in all of this? Like Qonce, East London falls under the ANC run Buffalo City Metropolitan Municipality.

VO 14 Almost a decade ago, the municipality established a development agency…with only one job: turning the area around.

VO 15 That entity… the Buffalo City Metropolitan Development Agency or BCMDA gets money from the municipality to boost economic development, tourism and investment…

LINK (Clip 489 / Day 1) This beachfront upgrade in East London was unveiled at the end of last year. It cost more than R100 million. It’s been dubbed the stoep by some locals and it's not hard to see why.

VO 16 Opposition councillors say what was delivered was NOT what was promised to the council. (photo of what was shown to council sent to you on Whatsapp)

UPSOUND Mziyanda Hlekiso / EFF Councillor (Clip 663 / Day 2) 01:40 This is a stoep, my man, this is a stoep. 01:49 The only thing that is missing here is the red or black paint.

VO 17 Opposition parties are angry. EFF councillor, Mziyanda Hlekiso, accused the BCMDA of wasting taxpayers’ money.

Time code HLEKISO 03:01 It went up and up and up until it costed us close to a million rand.


VO 18 The development agency….is also in charge of the Water World Upgrade…a place where what was imagined…children’s laughter and joy - is now just a faded memory.

VO 19 The overspend here is also eyewatering. Currently R14 million for a project that is far from complete.

GRAPHIC : Waterworld Upgrade
Initial contract value plus consultants fees R107,5 million / Actual expenditure to date: R121,5 million

VO 20 DA councillor, Sue Bentley, says costs for the Water World upgrade will probably escalate too.

UPSOUND Sue Bentley / DA Councillor (clip 649 / day 2) 05:24 And now they’re saying we don’t have more money but they wanting private investors for another 45,6 million, so eventually R170 million but with vandalism and theft happening there its going to escalate.

GOVAN: Time code 3:12 But, surely they’re not allowed to get away with doing that all the time?
UPSOUND Sue Bentley / DA Councillor Clip 649 / Day 2 Time code 03:16 Why are they not allowed to? Because the ANC is the majority here and things just go through and it’s very difficult to hold them to account. That’s why things happen the way they do happen.

VO 21 On the BCMDA - opposition councillors speak with one voice.

UPSOUND Mziyanda Hlekiso / EFF Councillor (Clip 663 / Day 2) Time code. 01:23 There is no accountability.Time code 03:34 Every month they are changing leaders, or the board of BCMDA.

VO 22 We wanted answers. Spokesperson Samkelo Ngwenya was tasked with speaking to us … on behalf of both the Municipality and the BCMDA.

GOVAN: Clip 673 / Day 3 Time code 01:10 Sam why are you doing this interview? Why isn’t the CEO Ayanda doing this interview?
UPSOUND Samkelo Ngwenya 01:29 Well I think they felt that lets have one voice particularly the fact that the agency reports to council. So in a way we wouldn’t want to contradict each other.

VO 23 And who really IS accountable? The BCMDA has been unstable for years.

GOVAN: Time code 9:22 Accountability works when people are retained. The BCMDA has a high turnover in leadership doesn’t it?
SAMKELO 9:30 It’s something that we have been concerned about, hence we appointed a CEO and stable board. No organisation wants a revolving door. 10:03 One of the things we have done in the agency is to suspend people who have not been competent enough.
GOVAN Clip 673 Time code: 11:11 Is the BC Municipality happy with how the BCMDA is conducting its work and running these projects?
SAMKELO 11:19 We’re comfortable
GOVAN: You really are comfortable?
SAMKELO Yes
GOVAN: With such huge overruns?
SAMKELO: Time code 11:30 This project has changed the face of our beachfront.If you remember what it was before. It used to be a parking lot.
GOVAN:Time code: 12:13 It’s a different design, how can you be proud of something that cost more and doesn’t look like what you ordered?
SAMKELO: Time code: 12:48 The artists impression is not the final approved design. They never went back to the people to tell them actually this is what has been approved.

VO 24 As for the Waterfront Upgrade, which started FIVE years ago, completion is clearly a long way off..

VO 25 Contractors walked off the site over a year ago, because of payment disputes, and the site has been left to the fate of the elements ever since.

LINK: (Clip 641 / Day 2) Pallets of fresh grass were delivered in 2022 just before an oversight visit, and they were intended for landscaping the water park.

UPSOUND Govan Day 3 / Clip 674 06:36 It looks nothing like it used to. It looks worse than it used to. That’s another area I used to go as a child. I’m telling you. It’s terrible, have you seen it?
UPSOUND Samkelo Ngwenya / Buffalo City Metro Municipality Spokesperson Clip 674 / Day 2 Time code: 07: 20 The contractor said to us they were at 95% almost finished, what we got and what we found there was a totally different picture.. 07:54 We’ve got a contractor there who misrepresented themselves. We’ve got a legal issue taking place. We are trying to fight by all means to just make sure that this issue is resolved..
UPSOUND: Samkelo: 15:41 If there is anyone out there who has got an issue, because this is taxpayers money, we’ll be the first to make those accountable they are held to book.
GOVAN 15:50 This is taxpayers money and the problem is the taxpayers are not happy.
SAM: Hence we have actually requested a report.

VO 26 The fate of Victoria Grounds also lies in the hands of the BCMDA. In 2019, the Municipality handed it over to the development agency to build a mix-use facility… including a shopping mall. Several years later, BCMDA appointed a developer. (Clip 659 on shots of the report / Day 2)

VO 27 Development of the mix-use facility has since stalled…

UPSOUND Thembani Tom / King Sports Veterans Association (Day 2 / Clip 543) 12:31 We had a meeting on 20 November, 2020 in Zwelitsha with BCMDA. We were fighting about this field. Somebody in our delegation referred to BCMDA as Buffalo City Destruction Agents. 13:01 Because of what they doing, everything they touch turns to stone.

VO 28 Exactly what is planned for the Victoria Grounds is unclear. The municipality says the BCMDA is in negotiations with the developer, and hopes the shopping mall can be built elsewhere.

UPSOUND Samkelo Ngwenya (Day 2 Clip 673)Time code 25:08 Unfortunately, when we looked at the alternative sites the contractor felt that it’s not going to add value. At the stage we’re in right now, we are trying to push the process so it can actually move faster. Time code 25:26 We really want a state of the art facility there and we are working towards that around the clock. Time code: 23:52 We are saying we’ve put plans in place, it’s a pity those plans have not materialised.
GOVAN Time code: 23:58 It’s not a pity, its just not good enough.
Samkelo: No I agree with you.
Govan: For decades, you maintained the Victoria grounds without a private partnership. And it was fine, it was the crown jewel of sports in Qonce.
Samkelo: That’s the challenge. It actually was not fine. It was running at a cost. Hence we felt that it would be much better in hands of people who could invest in it. And ultimately we make profit off it.

VO 29 Ngwenya insists not all of the BCMDA’s projects have been failures.

UPSOUND Samkelo Ngwenya Clip 673 Time code: 3:23 They’ve got six major projects. They’re not a hundred percent, but I mean I could give them a seven out of ten.
GOVAN: A seven out of ten, sir?
UPSOUND Samkelo: Absolutely.

VO 30 He denies the municipality is wasting taxpayers’ money.

UPSOUND Samkelo Ngwenya (Clip 674) Time code 25:28 And this is said without proof. Time code: 26:15 Councillors that are in council have access to every document and if there is anything unto that they find they should approach up to the level of law enforcement agencies to ensure it gets to the bottom of that. I do not think it’s the vision of government to take an agency and turn it into a cash cow for a political party. I think government set up the agency to ensure that it does projects for the people.

VO 31 In the end we did get to meet the CEO of the BCMDA - the mayor declined to be interviewed, but Ayanda Gqoboka agreed, only to cancel at the last minute.

NATSOUND (Clip 678 / Day 3) 00:44 Pleased to meet you. Ayanda Gqoboka. Govan: Why didn’t you want to speak to us? Ayanda: You had Samkelo and he dealt with you very well, he’s the head of communications. GOVAN: Yeah, well I did want to speak to you. Ayanda: The head of communications, he’s given you very good answers.

VO 32 The man who initially fobbed us off… did however allow us to film in his office…with sweeping views of the sea.

BREATHER

VO 33 For Thembani Tom, the agency meant to bring about meaningful change … has failed the people of this community.

UPSOUND Thembani Tom (Clip 543/ Day 2) 22:08 We have been deprived of better facilities by the Apartheid regime because of our colours, but now our own government is depriving us the facilities that we so fought for by not maintaining them and sell them for a quick profit. To me, a mall does not develop the people.

VO 34 These places hold such fond childhood memories for me…I would like to believe that there is still some hope in returning them to what they once were.…(visuals of Govan looking out to sea)

metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): An Eastern Cape development agency mandated to attract investors and increase economic development has come under the spotlight for a series of stalled multi-million rand projects.
metadata.Unique Selling Point: An Eastern Cape development agency, the Buffalo City Metropolitan Development Agency, has a series of failed multi-million rand projects on its track record. The BCMDA is funded by the Buffalo City Metropolitan Municipality to increase economic development and tourism. The Municipality has ploughed millions into its projects, but some have stalled, while others that have been completed have raised serious questions about why they cost so much.
metadata.Summary: The Buffalo City Metropolitan Municipality in the Eastern Cape is yet another municipality in South Africa that is failing to deliver services to its residents. Sewage spills have become commonplace, potholes pepper the roads, water cuts and poor water quality … these are just some of the issues residents deal with on a daily basis. Abandoned, hijacked buildings in the East London City Centre have become an eyesore and are fuelling crime. Driving through the centre, the dereliction and decay is visible everywhere. It’s clear the municipality is cash-strapped. But, that hasn’t stopped the Buffalo City Metropolitan Development Agency from cashing in on a number of multi million rand projects. The BCMDA is meant to drive development in the area, and its projects are funded by the Municipality. In this insert, we look at the BCMDA – and some of the multimillion rand projects its been involved in. In November last year, it unveiled a beachfront upgrade, that the EFF dubbed “The Stoep”. The project costs ballooned to R100 million and what was presented to council is not what was delivered. It is also involved in the upgrade of the Waterworld park which has cost R121 million to date. This project has completely stalled, and the BCMDA now says it needs over R40 million to complete it. The Victoria Grounds in Qonce, formerly King Williams Town, is also a project on BCMDA's books. They planned to demolish it and build a mall there and multi-use facility, but even that has stalled, despite a developer being contracted to do the job. The sports stadium, which has huge historical significance, has become a shell of what it once was and has been completely stripped. The ANC run municipality has been asked for reports on these projects, but are simply ignored. Opposition councillors say it’s impossible to get any information out of those in charge. In an attempt to find answers, we confront the Municipality. Both the current and former Mayor refused to do an interview with us. The BCMDA CEO cancelled a scheduled interview at the last minute, and instead Municipality spokesperson Samwelo Ngwenya was tasked with answering our questions on behalf of both the Municipality and the BCMDA.
